defold-astar - licence provenance, unresolved

This file records what each source actually says about the licence of
https://github.com/selimanac/defold-astar at revision
1471c5445b0c0376bd23c377e8ef8d84e52b43bf. The sources disagree, so they
are recorded separately rather than collapsed into a single claim. This
follows the same house rule used for the War Battles art provenance in
.agents/docs/research/war-battles-port-map.md. It is a source-provenance
record, not legal advice.

The project owner reviewed this discrepancy and decided to proceed with
ingestion of the extension's .script_api interface description.

1. The repository itself states nothing.
   The tree at 1471c5445b0c0376bd23c377e8ef8d84e52b43bf contains no
   LICENSE, LICENCE, COPYING, or equivalent file at any path, and
   README.md contains no licence statement. GitHub's licence API
   (https://api.github.com/repos/selimanac/defold-astar/license) returns
   HTTP 404, which is what that endpoint returns when it can detect no
   licence file. Verified 2026-09-18.

2. The Defold asset portal claims MIT.
   assets/apathfinding.json in defold/asset-portal at revision
   17a1f3d8a3f50e7840fbb6677465d1cb7799a15e records:

       "name": "A* Path Finding"
       "license": "MIT License"
       "project_url": "https://github.com/selimanac/defold-astar"

   That is the portal's own metadata claim. It is not corroborated by
   any file in the repository, and no MIT copyright line or permission
   text exists upstream to transcribe here.

3. The vendored pathfinder is zlib, not MIT.
   defold-astar vendors MicroPather (Lee Thomason) under
   astar/include/micropather/ and astar/src/. Its notice is the zlib
   licence and is reproduced verbatim in micropather-zlib.txt in this
   directory. That notice requires the origin of the software not be
   misrepresented and that the notice not be removed, so it carries its
   own attribution obligation independently of whatever terms cover
   defold-astar's own code.

Resolution
   Asking the author to add a LICENSE file to the repository would
   resolve this cleanly: it would replace the portal's second-hand claim
   with a first-party statement, and it would make the relationship
   between defold-astar's own terms and MicroPather's zlib terms
   explicit. Until that happens, the discrepancy stands as recorded
   above and must not be summarised as "MIT".

What this repository vendors from defold-astar
   Only astar/ext.manifest and astar/api/astar.script_api - the
   extension's interface description, checked in under
   tests/fixtures/defold-extension-ingestion/vendor/ so the ingestion
   test is offline, pinned, and reproducible. No defold-astar or
   MicroPather source code or headers are vendored. See
   extensions.lock.json in the fixture root for the exact file list,
   digests, and the upstream files that were deliberately not vendored.
